title: Augmented integral quotient comparisons and normalized Roos support
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$, $i\in I$, be a finite pairwise disjoint open and closed cover [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ and $R_i=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X_i}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and write $r_i$ for ordinary restriction on module sheaves, complexes and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $K\in D(R)$ and choose a quasi-isomorphism $q:P\to K$ with $P$ K-flat and with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. In the reduction tower [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] set $P_n=P\otimes_R(A_{E,n})_X$, read as an $R$-complex by the quotient projection, $\gamma_n(p)=p\otimes1$, and $\tau_n(p\otimes a)=p\otimes\rho_n(a)$ for the coefficient reduction $\rho_n:A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n}$. Restriction sends $q$ to an admissible K-flat flat-term resolution and gives chain isomorphisms
$$r_iP_n\cong r_iP\otimes_{R_i}(A_{E,n})_{X_i},\qquad p\otimes a\longmapsto r_ip\otimes r_ia,$$
commuting with $\gamma_n$ and $\tau_n$. Consequently the derived reduction isomorphism $r_i(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})\cong (r_iK)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], also after restricting scalars, identifies the actual maps $c_n=[\gamma_n][q]^{-1}$ and $t_n=[\tau_n]$ with the component reduction maps. These comparisons are natural on derived objects and morphisms.

Writing $K_n=\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$ and $c=(c_n)_n$, the derived categories admit countable products. Product and shift comparisons give a bijection between morphisms $\delta:\prod_nK_n\to K[1]$ and tuples $\delta_i:\prod_n(r_iK)_n\to(r_iK)[1]$; the triangle with arrows $c,1-s,\delta$ is distinguished exactly when each component triangle with its actual first map $(c_{i,n})_n$ is distinguished. The normalization is the canonical projection comparison, and the calculation applies to empty components and an empty partition.

proof.text: Use the extracted, completely proved integral Roos calculation for the tuple derived equivalence, canonical countable-product comparisons and reflection of the actual limit triangles. The original private integralRoosCalculus signature is preserved by applying this result.

Apply [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] to $R$: its coefficient identifications preserve $\pi_n$, $\rho_n$ and $1$. By [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus], restriction is exact, preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and preserves flatness and K-flatness. Thus $r_iq:r_iP\to r_iK$ is an admissible flat-term K-flat resolution. The same tensor comparison, with second factor $(A_{E,n})_X$ in degree zero, gives the asserted chain isomorphism $\beta_{i,n}:r_iP_n\to r_iP\otimes_{R_i}(A_{E,n})_{X_i}$ with the specified pure-tensor formula.

source.place: Definition 3.5.2, p. 24; agent finite-clopen application using the explicit reduction tower.

proof.text: The coefficient identifications give $\beta_{i,n}r_i\gamma_n(p)=r_ip\otimes1=\gamma_{i,n}(r_ip)$ and $\beta_{i,n}r_i\tau_n(p\otimes a)=r_ip\otimes\rho_{i,n}(r_ia)=\tau_{i,n}\beta_{i,n+1}(p\otimes a)$. These identities on local pure tensors determine the sheaf maps. Scalar restriction merely forgets part of the action, so preserves these equalities. Localize and compose the first identity with $[r_iq]^{-1}$: the maps $c_n$ and $t_n$ of [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] become precisely $c_{i,n}$ and $t_{i,n}$. The derived scalar comparisons of [lem-pur-clopen-derived-scalar-compositor] are natural for all derived morphisms and have exactly these chain representatives. Independence of the augmented tower from $q$ is [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined], which preserves both $c_n$ and $t_n$. Thus the calculation identifies the actual augmented towers, not only their level objects.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-clopen-strict-tower-roos-equivalence] to $C_n=P_n$ and $t_n=\tau_n$. It identifies products, their projections and $1-s$ with their component versions, and detects distinguishedness for the specified Roos triangle. By the fully faithful derived equivalence of [lem-pur-clopen-unbounded-derived-localization], a map $\delta:B\to K[1]$, $B=\prod_nK_n$, is equivalent to its tuple of component maps. Explicitly, if $\alpha_i:r_iB\cong B_i$ and $\sigma_i:r_i(K[1])\cong(r_iK)[1]$, the tuple is $\delta_i=\sigma_i r_i(\delta)\alpha_i^{-1}$. Conversely fullness gives a map from any such tuple, and faithfulness makes it unique. The product projections and Step 2 identify $r_i(c)$ with the actual component augmentation, so the distinguishedness assertion retains all three specified arrows.
